title: Mahmoud and Ehab and the bipartiteness
titleZh: Mahmoud 和 Ehab 与二分图
statementMd:
Mahmoud and Ehab continue their adventures! As everybody in the evil land knows, Dr. Evil likes bipartite graphs, especially trees.

A tree is a connected acyclic graph. A bipartite graph is a graph, whose vertices can be partitioned into $2$ sets in such a way, that for each edge $(*u*, *v*)$ that belongs to the graph, $*u*$ and $*v*$ belong to different sets. You can find more formal definitions of a tree and a bipartite graph in the notes section below.

Dr. Evil gave Mahmoud and Ehab a tree consisting of $*n*$ nodes and asked them to add edges to it in such a way, that the graph is still bipartite. Besides, after adding these edges the graph should be simple (doesn't contain loops or multiple edges). What is the maximum number of edges they can add?

A loop is an edge, which connects a node with itself. Graph doesn't contain multiple edges when for each pair of nodes there is no more than one edge between them. **A cycle and a loop aren't the same** .

## Input

The first line of input contains an integer $*n*$ — the number of nodes in the tree ($1 ≤ *n* ≤ 10^{5}$).

The next $*n* - 1$ lines contain integers $*u*$ and $*v*$ ($1 ≤ *u*, *v* ≤ *n*$, $*u* ≠ *v*$) — the description of the edges of the tree.

It's guaranteed that the given graph is a tree.

## Output

Output one integer — the maximum number of edges that Mahmoud and Ehab can add to the tree while fulfilling the conditions.

## Note

Tree definition: [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tree_(graph_theory)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tree_(graph_theory))

Bipartite graph definition: [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bipartite_graph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bipartite_graph)

In the first test case the only edge that can be added in such a way, that graph won't contain loops or multiple edges is $(2, 3)$, but adding this edge will make the graph non-bipartite so the answer is 0.

In the second test case Mahmoud and Ehab can add edges $(1, 4)$ and $(2, 5)$.
statementZhMd:
Mahmoud 和 Ehab 继续着他们的冒险！正如邪恶之地的所有人都知道的那样，邪恶博士喜欢二分图，尤其是树。

树是一种连通且无环的图。二分图是一种图，它的顶点可以被划分为 $2$ 个集合，使得对于图中的每条边 $(*u*, *v*)$，$*u*$ 和 $*v*$ 属于不同的集合。你可以在下面的说明部分找到树和二分图更形式化的定义。

邪恶博士给了 Mahmoud 和 Ehab 一棵由 $*n*$ 个节点组成的树，并要求他们向其中添加一些边，使得得到的图仍然是二分图。此外，添加边后的图应当是简单图（不包含自环或重边）。他们最多可以添加多少条边？

自环是连接一个节点自身的边。当对于每一对节点，它们之间至多有一条边时，图中不含重边。**环和自环并不是同一种东西**。

## 输入格式

输入的第一行包含一个整数 $*n*$ —— 树中节点的数量（$1 ≤ *n* ≤ 10^{5}$）。

接下来的 $*n* - 1$ 行包含两个整数 $*u*$ 和 $*v*$（$1 ≤ *u*, *v* ≤ *n*$，$*u* ≠ *v*$）——表示树中的一条边。

保证给出的图是一棵树。

## 输出格式

输出一个整数——在满足条件的情况下，Mahmoud 和 Ehab 最多可以向树中添加的边数。

## 说明

树的定义：[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tree_(graph_theory)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tree_(graph_theory))

二分图的定义：[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bipartite_graph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bipartite_graph)

在第一个测试用例中，唯一可以添加且不会使图包含自环或重边的边是 $(2, 3)$，但添加这条边会使图变成非二分图，因此答案是 0。

在第二个测试用例中，Mahmoud 和 Ehab 可以添加边 $(1, 4)$ 和 $(2, 5)$。
